top_stories.title: Okta moves inline to police what AI agents actually do
top_stories.summary: Okta has introduced an agent gateway designed to enforce authorization decisions for AI agents at runtime, moving beyond initial authentication to govern actions taken by autonomous AI agents once they have access. The gateway sits inline in the path of agent actions, enabling real-time policy enforcement on what AI agents can do within systems.

top_stories.title: Dual NetScaler Zero-Days Trigger Chaos for Citrix Customers
top_stories.summary: Citrix disclosed two critical zero-day vulnerabilities in its NetScaler products that affect default configurations and allow attackers unauthorized access to customer networks. The flaws are particularly relevant to IAM professionals as NetScaler is widely used for application delivery and access control, functioning as a gateway that manages authentication and session access.

top_stories.title: AI Agents Are Privileged Users; Who Is Auditing Their Access?
top_stories.summary: The article examines how autonomous AI agents are operating with broad privileged access in enterprise environments without the same auditing and oversight applied to human users. The piece frames AI agents as a emerging PAM and identity governance challenge, comparable to insider threat risks.

top_stories.title: JadePuffer AI Actor Compromises Azure Tenant in Destructive Cloud Attack
top_stories.summary: A threat actor dubbed "JadePuffer" compromised an Azure tenant in a destructive attack, deleting cloud-based storage, applications, and databases. The attacker reportedly used exposed credentials to gain initial access, highlighting risks around credential exposure and cloud identity security in Microsoft Azure environments.

top_stories.title: The Day-One Hole in Zero Trust Architecture
top_stories.summary: Specops has published an analysis identifying a structural vulnerability in Zero Trust architecture during the user onboarding phase, before credentials and MFA methods are established. The piece argues that identity verification must occur prior to credential issuance to close the trust gap that exists before strong authentication is in place.

news.title: Criminal recruiters want people on your payroll
news.summary: Intel 471's "Insiders for Hire" report details how cybercriminals actively recruit employees at targeted organizations to exploit their legitimate access privileges. The report covers underground markets where criminals pay brokers to find insiders who can perform actions like account resets, transaction approvals, and information lookups as sold services.

news.title: AI agents keep access to company data after their work is done
news.summary: Delinea's 2026 Identity Security Report: The AI Enforcement Gap found that IT teams are concerned about AI agents retaining access to company systems after completing their tasks. The report highlights a gap between written AI access policies and the ability to enforce them in real time when AI agents act on users' behalf.

news.title: Microsoft enables Windows settings backup by default for orgs
news.summary: Microsoft has enabled Windows settings backup and restore by default on all Microsoft Entra-joined or hybrid-joined enterprise systems upgraded to Windows 11 26H2. The change affects organizations using Microsoft Entra for device identity management and join configurations.

news.title: CISA Adds Exploited Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Auth Bypass to KEV
news.summary: CISA added a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-76504, CVSS 9.8) in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports of active exploitation. The flaw allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to access affected systems, representing a critical authentication control failure in network management infrastructure.

news.title: Citrix NetScaler Post-Exploitation Payload Creates Superuser, Maps Web Shell to CSS-Like URLs
news.summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical pre-authentication command injection vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway to deploy web shells and steal configuration data. The attacks involve creating superuser accounts and mapping web shells to CSS-like URLs, with LevelBlue's THOR team analyzing the exploitation activity across multiple customer environments.

news.title: From Shadow AI to Accountable Agents: Why Agent Governance Needs Enforcement
news.summary: The article addresses the challenge of governing AI agents within enterprise environments, arguing that identity governance frameworks must evolve beyond static models to continuously monitor and manage AI agent activity. The piece focuses on how traditional IAM and identity governance approaches need to adapt to handle non-human identities and autonomous AI agents operating across enterprise systems.

news.title: Over 543,000 valid credentials exposed in public GitHub repositories
news.summary: Over 543,000 valid credentials were found exposed in public GitHub repositories as of July, despite GitHub's existing security measures designed to prevent accidental credential leaks. The exposed credentials represent active authentication secrets that remain exploitable, raising concerns about secrets management practices across development environments.

news.title: Attackers Exploit Zimbra Flaw to Deploy Web Shells and Harvest Authentication Secrets
news.summary: Threat actors are exploiting a patched Zimbra Collaboration Suite vulnerability (CVE-2026-73570, CVSS 8.9) to deploy web shells and harvest authentication secrets from mailboxes. The flaw is an unauthenticated OS command injection vulnerability enabling remote code execution via SNMP, discovered by Microsoft Security Research.

news.title: Cisco Warns of Attackers Exploiting Critical Authentication Bypass in SD-WAN Manager
news.summary: Cisco has disclosed an actively exploited critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-76504) in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access the Manager's API with admin-level privileges, with fixed releases available but no workaround.

news.title: US-Focused CSuite Phishing Steals Microsoft 365 Sessions and Deploys RMM Tools for Remote Access
news.summary: Researchers at ANY.RUN identified the CSuite phishing campaign, which steals Microsoft 365 session tokens to bypass MFA and maintain persistent access. The campaign, analyzed across 351 sandbox submissions with 51% originating from the US, targets technology, manufacturing, government, and consulting sectors by combining session hijacking with remote management tool deployment.

news.title: keycloak v26.7.5
news.summary: Keycloak has released version 26.7.5 of its open source identity and access management platform. This is a maintenance/patch release of the widely-used IAM solution for modern applications and services.

news.title: CEO Interview: Oak
news.summary: Oak CEO Shai Ben-Zion Morag discusses the company's positioning in the identity governance market in an interview with CB Insights. The interview covers Oak's view of customer needs and their place within the identity governance space.

news.title: Britive Launches Frictionless PAM Transformation Program to Modernize Privileged Access for the Autonomous Era
news.summary: Britive has launched a Frictionless PAM Transformation Program aimed at helping enterprises migrate from traditional PAM environments to a modern authorization model. The program is designed to support AI agents, non-human identities, and cloud-native operations.

news.title: AI's Third Wave: Coworkers Break the Security Model That Worked for Agents
news.summary: Token Security has published analysis arguing that persistent AI "coworker" agents require dedicated identity constructs, including individual identities, defined owners, scoped permissions, and lifecycle management. The piece identifies a gap in existing security models, which were not designed to handle continuously operating AI entities with standing access rather than task-specific agents.

news.title: Microsoft to block Entra ID script injection attacks starting October
news.summary: Microsoft will implement protections against external script injection attacks in Entra ID authentication starting in October. The update targets script injection vulnerabilities within the Entra ID authentication system.

news.title: Security Uses Cryptography in Pieces. WinMagic Says That Gap Is What AI Attacks.
news.summary: WinMagic CEO Thi Nguyen-Huu argues that AI-enabled attacks exploit gaps between cryptographic security components, particularly the disconnect between authentication and the protected session that follows. The company's proposed approach focuses on reducing user-dependent security decisions and tightening the link between authentication and session security.

news.title: Five MCP Authentication Mechanisms Shipped in Two Weeks – the Pattern
news.summary: Five distinct authentication mechanisms for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) were shipped within a two-week window in late September, with none of the implementations coordinated or interoperable. Three independent security efforts converged simultaneously, resulting in fragmented authentication approaches for the emerging AI tool integration protocol.

news.title: NTT TechnoCross Receives Frost & Sullivan's 2026 Japanese Company of the Year Recognition for Privileged Access Management Leadership for the Third Consecutive Year
news.summary: NTT TechnoCross has received Frost & Sullivan's 2026 Japanese Company of the Year award in the privileged access management category for the third consecutive year. The recognition highlights the company's unified governance approach, cloud-ready security capabilities, and innovation in Japan's PAM market.

news.title: Could Be 36% Overvalued Following Its AI Agent Identity Push
news.summary: Aembit has announced support for Cross App Access, an open protocol introduced by Okta, positioning both companies within the AI agent identity space following Okta's Oktane 2026 announcements. The article examines Okta's valuation in the context of its AI agent identity strategy and the emerging ecosystem around its Cross App Access protocol.

news.title: French Tax Data Theft Using Stolen Staff Passwords Went Undetected for Seven Weeks
news.summary: An attacker used stolen staff credentials to exfiltrate tax data on hundreds of thousands of French taxpayers and businesses from France's tax administration over a seven-week period in June and July, going undetected by both the agency and ANSSI. ANSSI's post-incident report characterizes the attack as unsophisticated, attributing its success to weak password controls and insufficient monitoring of credential-based access.

news.title: Official MCP Python SDK Flaw Can Let Malicious Servers Steal OAuth Credentials
news.summary: A vulnerability in the official MCP Python SDK allowed malicious servers to steal OAuth credentials including client secrets, authorization codes, and PKCE proof keys by redirecting them to an attacker-controlled token endpoint. The flaw has been patched in SDK version 1.30.0 and later, according to a security advisory from maintainers.

news.title: In the AI era, identity evolves into the control plane for trust
news.summary: The article examines how identity is evolving to become the central control plane for trust in the AI era, shifting from human-centric authentication to managing AI agents and non-human identities. The piece addresses how traditional IAM frameworks must adapt to handle agentic AI systems that require authorization and access management controls.

news.title: Morgan Stanley Resets Okta Stock Price Target For Rest of Year
news.summary: Morgan Stanley issued a revised stock price target for Okta following the cybersecurity company's recent investor event. The updated target reflects the bank's increased conviction in Okta's positioning around securing AI agents.

news.title: AI agents spark an identity cleanup
news.summary: AI agents moving from pilots to production are forcing enterprises to re-examine their identity and access management infrastructure. The deployment rush is exposing legacy identity tool sprawl, integration costs, and security gaps accumulated over decades.

news.title: Securden Recognized as a Leader in GigaOm Radar for Enterprise Password Management
news.summary: Securden has been recognized as a Leader in the GigaOm Radar report for Enterprise Password Management. The recognition covers Securden's capabilities across password management, machine identities, and AI-agent governance within its unified identity security and privileged access management platform.

news.title: Catch threats before they escalate with real-time Identity Telemetry
news.summary: tenfold Software has published content explaining real-time identity telemetry as a complement to traditional identity governance periodic access reviews. The piece focuses on how continuous monitoring of identity activity can help security teams detect and investigate suspicious behavior before it escalates into a full breach.

news.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Flaws Could Expose AWS Credentials
news.summary: Security researchers discovered vulnerabilities in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's SDK that could allow attackers to execute commands within AI sandbox environments. The flaws potentially exposed AWS credentials accessible within those sandbox contexts.

news.title: Ghost Service Accounts Enable M365 Data Theft in Chile
news.summary: Ghost (forgotten/abandoned) service accounts in Microsoft 365 environments are being exploited to enable data theft in attacks targeting organizations in Chile. The attack vector highlights how unmanaged service accounts can bypass otherwise secured employee account controls, undermining an organization's entire M365 environment.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch update addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. AI is being credited for accelerating vulnerability discovery, though security experts note organizations are struggling to keep pace with testing and deploying the volume of fixes.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million drivers licenses from the US and Canada, apparently sourced from a Louisiana-based identity verification company. The FBI's New Orleans field office has launched an official inquiry into the breach, which involves a widely-used identity verification provider.
